You have to consider the statement and the assumptions and decide which of the assumption(s) is/are implicit in the statement. Statement Let us increase the taxes to cover the deficit. Assumptions I. The present taxes are very low. II. Deficit in a budget is not desirable. III. Deficit cannot be met without increasing the tax.
questions.questionHtml:
In the questions below, is given a statement followed by two assumptions numbered I and II. An assumption is something supposed or taken for granted. You have to consider the statement and the assumptions and decide which of the assumption(s) is/are implicit in the statement.

Statement Let us increase the taxes to cover the deficit.

Assumptions 

I. The present taxes are very low.

II. Deficit in a budget is not desirable.

III. Deficit cannot be met without increasing the tax.

options.text: If I and II are implicit
options.html: If I and II are implicit

options.text: If I and III are implicit
options.html: If I and III are implicit

options.text: If II and III are implicit
options.html: If II and III are implicit

questions.solution:
Statement: Let us increase the taxes to cover the deficit.

Assumptions 

I. The present taxes are very low ⇒ Not Implicit: The statement suggests increasing taxes to solve a specific problem (the deficit), but it doesn't imply that the current rate is "low." Taxes could already be high, but still insufficient to cover current spending.

II. Deficit in a budget is not desirable ⇒ Implicit: The proposal to increase taxes specifically to "cover the deficit" implies that the deficit is a problem that needs to be resolved or eliminated.

III. Deficit cannot be met without increasing the tax ⇒ Not Implicit: The statement proposes one method to cover the deficit, but it does not claim it is the only possible way (e.g., spending cuts could also be an option).

Hence, only Assumption II is implicit.

questions.question: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 45 × 10 - 125 ÷ 25 + 5 = 30
questions.questionHtml:
Which two signs should be interchanged to make the given equation correct?

45 × 10 - 125 ÷ 25 + 5 = 30
questions.solution:
BODMAS RULE:

We check the options one by one.

Option (1): ÷ and -

Given equation is: 45 × 10 - 125 ÷ 25 + 5 = 30 

After the sign interchange, the equation is: 45 × 10 ÷ 125 - 25 + 5 = 30 

⇒ 45 × 10 ÷ 125 - 25 + 5 = 30 

​⇒ 45 × 0.08 - 25 + 5 = 30

​⇒ 3.6 - 25 + 5 = 30 ​

​⇒ 8.6 - 25 = 30 

-16.4 ≠ 30 

LHS ≠ RHS

Option (2): × and -

Given equation is: 45 × 10 - 125 ÷ 25 + 5 = 30 

After the sign interchange, the equation is: 45 - 10 × 125 ÷ 25 + 5 = 30 

⇒ 45 - 10 × 125 ÷ 25 + 5 = 30 

⇒ 45 - 10 × 5 + 5 = 30 

⇒ 45 - 50 + 5 = 30  

⇒ 50 - 50 = 30

0 ≠ 30 

LHS ≠ RHS

Option (3):  - and + 

Given equation is: 45 × 10 - 125 ÷ 25 + 5 = 30 

After the sign interchange, the equation is: 45 × 10 + 125 ÷ 25 - 5 = 30 

⇒ 45 × 10 + 125 ÷ 25 - 5 = 30 

⇒  45 × 10 + 5 - 5 = 30 

⇒ 450 + 5 - 5 = 30

⇒ 455 - 5 = 30 

450 ≠ 30 

LHS ≠ RHS

Option (4): × and +

Given equation is: 45 × 10 - 125 ÷ 25 + 5 = 30 

After the sign interchange, the equation is: 45 + 10 - 125 ÷ 25 × 5 = 30 

⇒  45 + 10 - 125 ÷ 25 × 5 = 30

⇒ 45 + 10 - 5 × 5 = 30

⇒ 45 + 10 - 25 = 30

⇒ 55 - 25 = 30

30 = 30 

LHS = RHS

Hence, the correct answer is "× and +".

questions.questionHtml:
Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R):

Assertion (A): Sustainable Development supports the idea of the carrying capacity of the environment.

Reason (R): Carrying capacity is impacted by the availability of decomposers.

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is correct explanation of (A)
options.html: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is correct explanation of (A)

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not correct explanation of (A)
options.html: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not correct explanation of (A)
(A) is true, but (R) is false
(A) is false, but (R) is true

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2.

Key Points

  • Sustainable Development means the development that meets the needs of the present generation without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.
    • ​It stresses that the development and utilization of resources should be limited so that nature can regenerate them for the next generation.
    • It presumes that the development must be within the confines of the carrying capacity of ecosystems. Hence, statement 1 is correct.
  • Carrying capacity refers to the maximum population size that an environment can sustainably support without degrading the natural system.
  • Considering the carrying capacity of the environment while planning developmental programmes is of utmost necessity.
    • For example, if the population grows beyond the carrying capacity of Urban services, it will lead to the development of slums, pollution, unhygienic waste and sewage disposal, etc. It will negatively impact the living standards in urban areas.
    • Likewise, decomposers break down and recycle dead organisms and organic matter. 
      • They prevent the dead matter from accumulating and taking up space in the environment.
      • If their presence is diminished, environmental balance will disrupt.
      • The unhygienic condition leading to the emergence of various diseases will occur.
      • That's why the carrying capacity of the environment is impacted by decomposers. Hence, statement 2 is correct.
  • Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not correct explanation of (A).

questions.question: What is the arrangement between the caste and the village community for the supply of goods and services called?
questions.questionHtml: What is the arrangement between the caste and the village community for the supply of goods and services called?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is Jajmani system.

Key Points

  • Jajmani System: The term refers to a traditional economic and social arrangement found within certain caste-based societies, particularly in parts of rural India. This system is intricately linked with the village community structure and its functioning. Below are detailed points explaining the essence and functioning of the Jajmani System:
  • Community-Centric: At its core, the Jajmani System is deeply rooted in the community life of a village. It revolves around mutual dependencies and the fulfillment of various needs within a village community, ensuring that all members have access to essential goods and services.
  • Caste-Based Occupations: Traditionally, specific castes were associated with particular occupations. This meant that each caste had a defined role within the village economy, contributing goods or services that were essential for the daily life of the community. For example, a certain caste might be responsible for agriculture, another for pottery, and yet another for weaving.
  • Exchange of Services and Goods: Unlike modern economies that are heavily reliant on monetary transactions, the Jajmani System facilitated an exchange of goods and services based on social obligations and traditional practices. This could involve barter systems or the provision of services in exchange for protection, food, or other goods.
  • Social Cohesion and Support: This system played a vital role in fostering social cohesion and interdependence among different castes within a village. It ensured that even in times of scarcity or economic hardship, the basic needs of the community members were met through a collective support system.
  • Cultural and Social Norms: The functioning of the Jajmani System was deeply intertwined with cultural and social norms. It was governed by a set of unwritten rules and traditions that dictated the interactions between different castes and the nature of the exchanges that took place.
  • Evolution and Challenges: With the advent of modernization, industrialization, and changes in the economic landscape, the traditional Jajmani System has faced significant challenges. However, traces of this system can still be found in some rural communities, where it continues to influence social and economic interactions.

questions.question: What is the name of High-speed Expendable Aerial Target (HEAT), developed by ADE division of DRDO?
questions.questionHtml: What is the name of High-speed Expendable Aerial Target (HEAT), developed by ADE division of DRDO?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is ABHYAS.

Key Points

  • ABHYAS is a High-speed Expendable Aerial Target (HEAT) developed by the Aeronautical Development Establishment (ADE), a division of the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) in India.
  • The system is designed to serve as a target for evaluation of various missile systems, including surface-to-air and air-to-air missiles.
  • ABHYAS uses a gas turbine engine for propulsion and is equipped with an inertial navigation system (INS) based on a MEMS (Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems) configuration.
  • The target is launched using a twin booster system, which provides initial acceleration, and it can achieve speeds up to 0.5 Mach.
  • It is capable of simulating a variety of aerial threats for testing and training purposes, making it a crucial component of India's defense preparedness.

Additional Information

  • Gas Turbine Engine: ABHYAS is powered by a small gas turbine engine, which ensures sustained flight at high speeds and altitudes, essential for simulating real threats.
  • Inertial Navigation System (INS): The MEMS-based INS provides precise control and navigation, allowing the target to follow pre-programmed flight paths or real-time commands.
  • Advanced Design: ABHYAS features a fuselage made of lightweight composite materials, enhancing its aerodynamics and efficiency.
  • Testing Applications: The platform is used extensively for testing radar systems, weapon systems, and pilot training in intercepting aerial threats.
  • Indigenous Development: As a product of DRDO, ABHYAS highlights India's capability in developing state-of-the-art defense technologies and reducing dependency on foreign systems.

Key Points

  • Statement 1 is incorrect: The Peninsular India does not have a well-defined cold weather season due to its tropical climate. Winters are mild and less pronounced compared to northern India.
  • Statement 2 is correct: Coastal areas in India experience minimal seasonal variation in temperature, primarily due to the moderating effect of the surrounding seas.
  • The Peninsular region is influenced by tropical climatic conditions, where temperature variations across seasons are relatively smaller.
  • Coastal areas benefit from the maritime influence, which keeps temperatures relatively uniform throughout the year.
  • Regions closer to the equator, like southern India, experience less seasonal temperature fluctuation compared to regions farther from the equator.

Additional Information

  • Climatic Zones in India:
    • India has six major climatic zones: Tropical Rainforest, Tropical Monsoon, Tropical Savanna, Hot Desert, Mountain, and Humid Subtropical.
    • The Peninsular region largely falls under the Tropical Monsoon climate type.
  • Maritime Influence: Coastal areas experience maritime influence, which moderates extreme temperatures, resulting in mild winters and summers.
  • Seasonal Variations: Northern India experiences distinct seasons (summer, monsoon, winter), while the southern peninsula has less pronounced seasonal changes due to its proximity to the equator.
  • Western Coastal Plains: These regions, including places like Kerala and Goa, have consistent temperatures throughout the year, with high humidity levels.
  • Rainfall Pattern: Coastal regions experience significant rainfall during the monsoon season, but the temperature remains consistent due to the ocean’s stabilizing effect.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a primary factor affecting the variation of Insolation on Earth?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is NOT a primary factor affecting the variation of Insolation on Earth?

options.text: Presence of water bodies in an area
options.html: Presence of water bodies in an area

options.text: Rotation of the Earth on its axis
options.html: Rotation of the Earth on its axis

options.text: Angle of inclination of the Sun's rays
options.html: Angle of inclination of the Sun's rays

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Presence of water bodies in an area.

Key Points

  • Insolation refers to the amount of solar radiation received by the Earth's surface.
  • The variation in insolation is primarily determined by factors such as the angle of the Sun’s rays, Earth’s rotation, and atmospheric transparency.
  • The angle of inclination of the Sun’s rays impacts the intensity and distribution of solar energy, with higher angles resulting in more concentrated energy.
  • The rotation of the Earth causes daily variations in insolation, leading to the alternation of day and night.
  • Transparency of the atmosphere affects how much solar energy reaches the surface, as clouds, dust, and pollutants can block or scatter sunlight.

Additional Information

  • Primary Factors Affecting Insolation:
    • The Earth’s axial tilt (~23.5°) causes seasonal variations in insolation.
    • The Earth's shape, being an oblate spheroid, results in uneven solar energy distribution.
    • Latitude influences insolation, with regions near the equator receiving more consistent and intense solar energy.
  • Earth’s Atmosphere and Insolation:
    • The atmosphere filters solar radiation, absorbing harmful UV rays through the ozone layer.
    • Cloud cover and atmospheric conditions such as aerosols influence the amount of insolation reaching the Earth’s surface.
  • Solar Constant:
    • The solar constant is the average amount of solar energy received per unit area at the top of the Earth's atmosphere, approximately 1,366 watts per square meter.
    • It provides a reference for understanding energy input from the Sun.
  • Factors NOT Primarily Affecting Insolation:
    • The presence of water bodies affects local climate and heat retention but does not directly influence the variation of insolation.
    • Topography and vegetation also modify local heating but are secondary factors in insolation variation.

questions.question: Which instrument is used to measure the intensity of light produced by an unknown source in terms of a standard source?
questions.questionHtml: Which instrument is used to measure the intensity of light produced by an unknown source in terms of a standard source?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Photometer.

Key Points

  • Photometer:
    • A photometer is an instrument used to measure the intensity of light.
    • It quantifies the amount of light, whether visible or other portions of the electromagnetic spectrum.
    • Photometers are used in various fields, including photography, astronomy, and environmental science.
    • They can measure the absolute intensity of a light source or compare the relative intensities of two sources.
    • Some photometers are designed to measure light intensity over a specific area or from a particular direction.
    • Different types of photometers exist, each suited for specific applications and light conditions.
    • They often utilize sensors that convert light into an electrical signal, which is then processed and displayed as a light intensity value.

Additional Information

  • Calipers:
    • Calipers are precision measuring instruments used to determine the distance between two points.
    • They are commonly used in engineering, manufacturing, and metalworking to measure the dimensions of objects with high accuracy.
    • Calipers typically consist of a main scale with a sliding jaw that can be adjusted to fit the object being measured.
    • Different types of calipers exist, including vernier calipers, dial calipers, and digital calipers, each offering varying levels of precision and ease of use.
    • Calipers measure lengths, widths, depths, and diameters.
    • They are not used to measure light intensity.
  • Dynamometer:
    • A dynamometer is an instrument used to measure force, torque, or power.
    • They are commonly used in engineering and automotive applications to test the performance of engines, motors, and other mechanical systems.
    • Dynamometers can measure the force exerted by a machine or the torque it produces.
    • They are also used in fitness and rehabilitation to measure muscle strength.
    • Dynamometers come in various forms, each designed for specific types of measurements.
    • They are not related to measuring light.
  • Ammeter:
    • An ammeter is an instrument used to measure electric current in a circuit.
    • It is connected in series with the circuit element whose current is being measured.
    • Ammeters are essential tools in electrical engineering and electronics for diagnosing circuit problems and ensuring proper operation of electrical devices.
    • They typically display the current in amperes (A).
    • Different types of ammeters exist, including analog ammeters and digital ammeters.
    • Ammeters measure the flow of electric charge and are not used to measure light intensity.

questions.question: Fill in the blank:The devotional composition “Guru Bin Kaun Bataaye” is commonly rendered in the tala known as ____
questions.questionHtml: Fill in the blank:The devotional composition “Guru Bin Kaun Bataaye” is commonly rendered in the tala known as ____
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Teentaal.

Key Points

  • The devotional composition “Guru Bin Kaun Bataaye” is commonly rendered in the tala known as Teentaal. It is one of the most widely used and versatile talas in Hindustani classical music.
  • Teentaal consists of 16 beats, divided into four equal sections (vibhags) of four beats each.
  • This tala is known for its balanced structure, making it suitable for both vocal and instrumental performances, as well as for compositions such as devotional songs.
  • The first beat of Teentaal is called Sam, and it marks the most emphasized point in the tala cycle, serving as a reference for rhythm.
  • Teentaal is commonly used in compositions like khayals, bhajans, thumris, and even instrumental renditions, showcasing its adaptability in classical music.

Additional Information

  • Other Talas in Hindustani Music:
    • Keharwa: This tala has 8 beats divided into two vibhags of 4 beats each. It is predominantly used in light classical and folk music forms like bhajans and ghazals.
    • Dadra: It consists of 6 beats, divided into two vibhags (3 + 3). This tala is commonly employed in lighter genres such as thumris and dadra compositions.
    • Roopak: This tala is unique with 7 beats, divided into three vibhags (3 + 2 + 2). It is frequently used in semi-classical and classical music, as well as in instrumental performances.
  • Significance of Tala in Indian Music:
    • Tala is the rhythmic framework in Indian classical music that determines the time cycle of a composition.
    • It provides a structured and recurring rhythmic pattern, allowing performers to synchronize their music.
    • Different talas are suited to different genres and moods, contributing to the overall aesthetic experience of the performance.
  • Important Features of Teentaal:
    • Bol Pattern: The basic bols (syllables) of Teentaal are Dha Dhin Dhin Dha, Dha Dhin Dhin Dha, Dha Tin Tin Ta, Ta Dhin Dhin Dha.
    • Usage: Teentaal is highly versatile and is used in a wide range of musical compositions, from classical to semi-classical and devotional music.
    • Universality: Its balanced structure makes it a favorite among artists for showcasing intricate rhythmic patterns and improvisations.
  • Role of Tala in Devotional Music:
    • Devotional songs often use talas that are easy to follow, such as Teentaal and Keharwa, to enhance the listener's spiritual experience.
    • The repetitive and cyclical nature of talas helps create a meditative atmosphere, making them suitable for bhajans and kirtans.

questions.question: Generally the correct sequence of atmospheric layers with increasing heights is
questions.questionHtml: Generally the correct sequence of atmospheric layers with increasing heights is
questions.solution:

Key Points

  • The atmosphere is divided into layers based on temperature gradients, with the sequence being Troposphere, Stratosphere, Mesosphere, and Thermosphere as height increases.
  • The Troposphere is the lowest layer, extending up to approximately 8-15 km, where most weather phenomena occur.
  • The Stratosphere lies above the Troposphere, extending up to about 50 km, and contains the ozone layer that absorbs harmful UV radiation.
  • The Mesosphere extends from 50 km to 85 km and is the layer where meteors burn upon entering Earth’s atmosphere.
  • The Thermosphere, above the Mesosphere, extends up to 600 km and is characterized by high temperatures due to solar radiation absorption.

Additional Information

  • Troposphere:
    • It contains approximately 75% of the atmosphere's mass.
    • Temperature decreases with altitude in this layer.
    • Most clouds and precipitation occur in the Troposphere.
  • Stratosphere:
    • Temperature increases with altitude due to the presence of the ozone layer.
    • Commercial aircraft often cruise in this layer for smoother flights.
  • Mesosphere:
    • It is the coldest atmospheric layer, with temperatures dropping as low as -90°C.
    • This layer protects Earth by burning up meteoroids.
  • Thermosphere:
    • Temperatures can exceed 2000°C due to solar radiation absorption.
    • The International Space Station orbits within this layer.
  • Exosphere:
    • It is the outermost layer of Earth's atmosphere, transitioning into space.
    • Particles in the Exosphere are sparse and move freely due to weak gravitational forces.

questions.question: For A = 30°, find the value of: \(\frac{-3\sin^22A+2\sec^2A-\tan\frac{3A}{2}}{\frac{1}{3}\sin3A}\)
questions.questionHtml: For A = 30°, find the value of: \(\frac{-3\sin^22A+2\sec^2A-\tan\frac{3A}{2}}{\frac{1}{3}\sin3A}\)
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Substitute A = 30° directly into the given expression.

Numerator = −3×sin260° + 2×sec230° − tan45° = −3×(3/4) + 2×(4/3) − 1 = −7/12.

Denominator = (1/3)×sin90° = 1/3.

Result = (−7/12) ÷ (1/3) = −7/4.

∴ The correct answer is −7/4.

Alternate Method

Given:

A = 30°

Expression: [−3sin22A + 2sec2A − tan(3A/2)] / [(1/3)sin3A]

Calculation:

⇒ Substitute A = 30° into the individual terms:

⇒ sin(2A) = sin(2 × 30°) = sin(60°) = √3/2

⇒ sec(A) = sec(30°) = 2/√3

⇒ tan(3A/2) = tan(3 × 30° / 2) = tan(45°) = 1

⇒ sin(3A) = sin(3 × 30°) = sin(90°) = 1

⇒ Now substitute these values back into the expression:

⇒ Numerator = −3×(√3/2)2 + 2×(2/√3)2 − 1

⇒ Numerator = −3×(3/4) + 2×(4/3) − 1

⇒ Numerator = −9/4 + 8/3 − 1

⇒ LCM of 4 and 3 is 12.

⇒ Numerator = (−27 + 32 − 12) / 12 = −7/12

⇒ Denominator = (1/3) × 1 = 1/3

⇒ Final Value = (−7/12) / (1/3)

⇒ Final Value = (−7/12) × 3 = −7/4

∴ The correct answer is −7/4.

Additional Information

Standard Trigonometric Values

For standard angles: sin(30°) = 1/2, sin(60°) = √3/2, sin(90°) = 1. The tangent of 45° is always 1.

Reciprocal Identities

sec(θ) = 1/cos(θ), cosec(θ) = 1/sin(θ), and cot(θ) = 1/tan(θ). Since cos(30°) = √3/2, sec(30°) = 2/√3.

Basic Trigonometric Identities

sin2(θ) + cos2(θ) = 1, 1 + tan2(θ) = sec2(θ), and 1 + cot2(θ) = cosec2(θ).

questions.question: A metal sphere of 8 cm radius is melted and small balls of radius 0.5 cm are being made from it. The number of small balls are -
questions.questionHtml: A metal sphere of 8 cm radius is melted and small balls of radius 0.5 cm are being made from it. The number of small balls are -
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

When a 3D object is melted and recast into smaller objects, the number of objects formed is the ratio of their volumes.

For spheres, the formula directly simplifies to the cube of the ratio of their radii.

Number of balls = (R ÷ r)3

⇒ Number of balls = (8 ÷ 0.5)3 = 163 = 4096

∴ The correct answer is 4096 balls.

Alternate Method

Given:

Radius of large metal sphere (R) = 8 cm

Radius of small ball (r) = 0.5 cm

Formula Used:

Volume of a sphere = 4/3 × π × (radius)3

Number of small balls = Volume of large sphere ÷ Volume of small ball

Calculations:

⇒ Volume of large metal sphere = 4/3 × π × 83 cm3

⇒ Volume of one small ball = 4/3 × π × 0.53 cm3

⇒ Number of small balls = (4/3 × π × 83) ÷ (4/3 × π × 0.53)

By canceling common terms (4/3 × π):

⇒ Number of small balls = 83 ÷ 0.53

⇒ Number of small balls = 512 ÷ 0.125

⇒ Number of small balls = 4096

∴ The correct answer is 4096 balls.

Additional Information

Principle of Melting and Recasting

When a solid object is melted and reshaped into one or more objects, the total volume of the material remains constant before and after the process.

Volume of a Sphere

The amount of space contained within a sphere of radius r is calculated using the formula V = 4/3 × π × r3.

Surface Area of a Sphere

The total outer surface area of a sphere with radius r is given by the formula A = 4 × π × r2.

questions.question: The age of a student is 50% more than the other student. If there is a difference of 6 years in their ages, then the age of the elder student is:
questions.questionHtml: The age of a student is 50% more than the other student. If there is a difference of 6 years in their ages, then the age of the elder student is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let younger student age be 100%.

Elder student age = 100% + 50% = 150%.

Ratio of their ages = 150 : 100 = 3 : 2.

Difference in ratio = 3 − 2 = 1 unit.

1 unit = 6 years ⇒ Elder student age = 3 × 6 = 18 years.

∴ The correct answer is 18 years.

Alternate Method

Given:

Elder student age = 50% more than younger student.

Difference in ages = 6 years.

Calculations:

⇒ Let the age of the younger student be x years.

⇒ Age of the elder student = x + (50% of x) = x + 0.5x = 1.5x years.

⇒ Difference in their ages = 1.5x − x = 0.5x

⇒ Given difference = 6 years

⇒ 0.5x = 6

⇒ x = 6 ÷ 0.5 = 12 years.

⇒ Age of the elder student = 1.5 × 12 = 18 years.

∴ The correct answer is 18 years.

Additional Information

Ratio & Proportion Basics

When one value is A% more than another, their ratio is (100 + A) : 100.

Age Problems

The difference in ages of two people always remains constant over time. If the ratio of their present ages is a : b, the absolute difference is |a − b| parts.

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

50% is equivalent to 1/2. Therefore, 50% more translates directly to a multiplier of 1 + 1/2 = 3/2.

questions.question: Three equal circles each of diameter d are drawn on a plane in such a way that each circle touches the other two circles. A big circle is drawn in such a manner that it touches each of the small circles internally. The area of the big circle is
questions.questionHtml: Three equal circles each of diameter d are drawn on a plane in such a way that each circle touches the other two circles. A big circle is drawn in such a manner that it touches each of the small circles internally. The area of the big circle is
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For three mutually tangent equal circles of radius r, the circumscribing circle has radius R = r(2/√3 + 1).

Given the diameter is d, the radius of the small circles is r = d/2.

⇒ Radius of large circle (R) = (d/2) × [(2 + √3) / √3] = d(2 + √3) / (2√3)

⇒ Area of large circle = πR2 = π × [d(2 + √3) / (2√3)]2 = πd2(√3 + 2)2 / 12

∴ The correct answer is πd2(√3 + 2)2 / 12 sq. units.

Alternate Method

Given:

Three equal circles of diameter d.

Radius of each small circle (r) = d/2.

Formula Used:

When three equal circles touch externally, their centers form an equilateral triangle with side = 2r.

Circumradius of an equilateral triangle = Side ÷ √3.

Calculations:

⇒ Side of the equilateral triangle = 2 × (d/2) = d.

⇒ The centroid (O) of the triangle is equidistant from all three centers.

⇒ Distance from O to the center of any small circle (C₁) = d / √3.

⇒ The large circle touches the small circles internally.

⇒ Radius of the large circle (R) = Distance (O to C₁) + Radius of small circle (C₁ to P).

⇒ R = d/√3 + d/2

⇒ R = [2d + √3d] / (2√3) = d(2 + √3) / (2√3)

⇒ Area of the large circle = πR2

⇒ Area = π × [d(2 + √3) / (2√3)]2

⇒ Area = π × d2(2 + √3)2 / 12

∴ The correct answer is πd2(√3 + 2)2 / 12 sq. units.

Additional Information

Circumcircle of an Equilateral Triangle

The radius of a circle passing through all three vertices of an equilateral triangle of side a is given by R = a / √3.

Incircle of an Equilateral Triangle

The radius of a circle tangent to all three sides of an equilateral triangle of side a is given by r = a / (2√3).

Tangency of Circles

When two circles touch externally, the distance between their centers is r1 + r2. When they touch internally, the distance is |r1 − r2|.

questions.question: A man completes half of a trip at 30 miles per hours and the other half at 60 miles per hour. If the whole trip is 20 miles, how much time will eh take to complete the trip?
questions.questionHtml: A man completes half of a trip at 30 miles per hours and the other half at 60 miles per hour. If the whole trip is 20 miles, how much time will eh take to complete the trip?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

When a trip is divided into two equal distances covered at speeds x and y, the average speed is (2 × x × y) ÷ (x + y).

Average speed = (2 × 30 × 60) ÷ (30 + 60) = 3600 ÷ 90 = 40 mph.

Total distance = 20 miles.

Total time = Total distance ÷ Average speed = 20 ÷ 40 = 1/2 hour.

Time in minutes = 1/2 × 60 = 30 minutes.

∴ The correct answer is 30 minute.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total distance = 20 miles

Distance of 1st half (D1) = 20 ÷ 2 = 10 miles, Speed (S1) = 30 mph

Distance of 2nd half (D2) = 20 ÷ 2 = 10 miles, Speed (S2) = 60 mph

Formula Used:

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Total Time = t1 + t2

Calculations:

⇒ Time for 1st half (t1) = 10 ÷ 30 = 1/3 hour

⇒ Time for 2nd half (t2) = 10 ÷ 60 = 1/6 hour

⇒ Total Time = 1/3 + 1/6 = 2/6 + 1/6 = 3/6 = 1/2 hour

⇒ Total Time in minutes = 1/2 × 60 = 30 minutes

∴ The correct answer is 30 minute.

Additional Information

Average Speed for Equal Distances

When a journey is divided into equal halves covered at speeds S1 and S2, the average speed is calculated using the harmonic mean: (2 × S1 × S2) ÷ (S1 + S2).

Average Speed for Equal Time

When a journey is divided into equal time intervals covered at speeds S1 and S2, the average speed is simply the arithmetic mean: (S1 + S2) ÷ 2.

Relative Speed Concept

When two bodies move in the same direction, their relative speed is S1 − S2. When they move in opposite directions, their relative speed is S1 + S2.

questions.question: Three cubes of a metal whose edges are in the ratio 3 ∶ 4 ∶ 5 are melted and converted into a single cube whose diagonal is 12√3 cm. Find the edges of the three cubes.
questions.questionHtml: Three cubes of a metal whose edges are in the ratio 3 ∶ 4 ∶ 5 are melted and converted into a single cube whose diagonal is 12√3 cm. Find the edges of the three cubes.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The volumes of cubes with edges in the ratio 3  ∶ 4  ∶ 5 are proportional to 33  ∶ 43  ∶ 53 = 27  ∶ 64  ∶ 125.

Total volume of the melted cubes = 27 + 64 + 125 = 216 parts, which equals the volume of the single new cube.

The edge of the new single cube will be 3√216 = 6 parts.

Given the diagonal of the new cube = a√3 = 12√3 ⇒ a = 12.

So, 6 parts = 12 ⇒ 1 part = 2.

Edges of the three cubes = (3 × 2), (4 × 2), (5 × 2) = 6 units, 8 units, 10 units.

∴ The correct answer is 6 units, 8 units, 10 units.

Alternate Method

Given:

Ratio of edges of three cubes = 3  ∶ 4  ∶ 5

Diagonal of the new single cube = 12√3 cm

Formula Used:

Volume of a cube = a3 (where a is the edge)

Diagonal of a cube = a√3

Calculations:

⇒ Let the edges of the three cubes be 3x, 4x, and 5x respectively.

⇒ Sum of volumes of three cubes = (3x)3 + (4x)3 + (5x)3

⇒ Sum of volumes = 27x3 + 64x3 + 125x3 = 216x3

⇒ Let the edge of the newly formed single cube be a.

⇒ Volume of the new cube = a3 = 216x3

⇒ a = 3√(216x3) = 6x

⇒ Given that the diagonal of the new single cube is 12√3.

⇒ a√3 = 12√3

⇒ 6x√3 = 12√3

⇒ 6x = 12

⇒ x = 2

⇒ First cube edge = 3x = 3 × 2 = 6 units

⇒ Second cube edge = 4x = 4 × 2 = 8 units

⇒ Third cube edge = 5x = 5 × 2 = 10 units

∴ The correct answer is 6 units, 8 units, 10 units.

Additional Information

Volume of a Cube

The amount of space occupied by a 3D cube. It is calculated as V = a3, where a is the length of the edge.

Diagonal of a Cube

The longest segment connecting two opposite corners of a cube passing through its center. Its length is equal to a√3.

Conservation of Volume

When one or more solid shapes are melted and recast into a single new shape, the total volume remains constant during the transformation process.

questions.question: If the length of side of a cube is increased by \(44 \frac{4}{9}\%\) then find the approximate difference between the numerical value of percentage increase in its volume and percentage increase in its total surface area?
questions.questionHtml: If the length of side of a cube is increased by \(44 \frac{4}{9}\%\) then find the approximate difference between the numerical value of percentage increase in its volume and percentage increase in its total surface area?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The fractional value of 44 4/9% is 4/9, meaning the side of the cube increases from 9 to 13 units.

Area ratio = 92 : 132 = 81 : 169 → % Increase = (88 ÷ 81) × 100 ≈ 108.64%

Volume ratio = 93 : 133 = 729 : 2197 → % Increase = (1468 ÷ 729) × 100 ≈ 201.37%

Difference in % increase = 201.37% − 108.64% = 92.73% ≈ 92.

∴ The correct answer is 92.

Alternate Method

Given:

Percentage increase in the side of the cube = 44 4/9%

⇒ Fractional value = (400 ÷ 9) × (1 ÷ 100) = 4/9

Let the original side of the cube be 9 units.

⇒ New side of the cube = 9 + 4 = 13 units

Calculations:

⇒ Ratio of sides = 9 : 13

⇒ Total Surface Area ratio = 92 : 132 = 81 : 169

⇒ Percentage increase in Total Surface Area = [(169 − 81) ÷ 81] × 100 = (88 ÷ 81) × 100 ≈ 108.64%

⇒ Volume ratio = 93 : 133 = 729 : 2197

⇒ Percentage increase in Volume = [(2197 − 729) ÷ 729] × 100 = (1468 ÷ 729) × 100 ≈ 201.37%

⇒ Required Difference = 201.37% − 108.64% = 92.73%

⇒ The closest approximate value is 92.

∴ The correct answer is 92.

Additional Information

Scale Factors in Mensuration

When the linear dimensions (like side or radius) of a 3D object are scaled by a ratio a : b, the surface area scales by the ratio a2 : b2, and the volume scales by the ratio a3 : b3.

Percentage Increase

Percentage increase is always calculated on the base or original value using the formula: % Increase = (Difference ÷ Original Value) × 100.

questions.question: An automobile financer claims to be lending money at simple interest, but he includes the interest every six months for calculating the principal. If he is charging an interest at the rate of 10%, the effective rate of interest becomes
questions.questionHtml: An automobile financer claims to be lending money at simple interest, but he includes the interest every six months for calculating the principal. If he is charging an interest at the rate of 10%, the effective rate of interest becomes
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Adding interest to the principal every 6 months is equivalent to half-yearly compounding.

Half-yearly rate = 10% ÷ 2 = 5%

Effective annual rate formula = a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100

Effective rate = 5 + 5 + (5 × 5) ÷ 100

Effective rate = 10 + 0.25 = 10.25%

∴ The correct answer is 10.25%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Rate of simple interest (R) = 10% per annum

Interest is added to the principal every 6 months.

Formula Used:

Simple Interest (I) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Calculations:

⇒ Let the initial principal (P) be ₹100.

⇒ Rate for half-year = 10% ÷ 2 = 5% and Time (T) = 1 half-year.

⇒ Interest for first 6 months = (100 × 5 × 1) ÷ 100 = ₹5

⇒ New principal after 6 months = 100 + 5 = ₹105

⇒ Interest for next 6 months = (105 × 5 × 1) ÷ 100 = ₹5.25

⇒ Total interest earned in 1 year = 5 + 5.25 = ₹10.25

⇒ Effective rate of interest = (10.25 ÷ 100) × 100% = 10.25%

∴ The correct answer is 10.25%.

Additional Information

Half-Yearly Compounding

When interest is compounded half-yearly, the rate is halved and the time period is doubled. Formula: A = P(1 + R/200)2T.

Quarterly Compounding

When interest is compounded quarterly, the rate is divided by 4 and the time period is multiplied by 4. Formula: A = P(1 + R/400)4T.

Effective Rate of Interest

It is the actual annual interest rate that incorporates compounding within the year. For rate r% compounded n times a year: Effective Rate = [(1 + r/100n)n − 1] × 100.

questions.question: 8 men and 12 women can build a wall in 10 days. 6 men and 8 women can build the same in 14 days. How long will take 1 woman to build it alone?
questions.questionHtml: 8 men and 12 women can build a wall in 10 days. 6 men and 8 women can build the same in 14 days. How long will take 1 woman to build it alone?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Using the chain rule formula: M1 × D1 = M2 × D2

10 × (8M + 12W) = 14 × (6M + 8W)

80M + 120W = 84M + 112W ⇒ 4M = 8W ⇒ 1M = 2W

Total Work in terms of women's efficiency = 10 × (8 × 2W + 12W) = 280W

Time taken by 1 woman alone = 280W ÷ 1W = 280 days

∴ The correct answer is 280 days.

Alternate Method

Given:

8 men and 12 women can build a wall in 10 days.

6 men and 8 women can build the same in 14 days.

Formula Used:

Total Work = Efficiency × Time

Person Days Total Work Efficiency
8 Men + 12 Women 10 70 7
6 Men + 8 Women 14 5

Calculations:

Let the efficiency of 1 man be M and 1 woman be W.

⇒ 8M + 12W = 7   ... (i)

⇒ 6M + 8W = 5   ... (ii)

Multiplying equation (i) by 3 and equation (ii) by 4 to equate the men's efficiency:

⇒ 24M + 36W = 21

⇒ 24M + 32W = 20

Subtracting the second equation from the first:

⇒ 4W = 1 ⇒ W = 1/4

The efficiency of 1 woman is 1/4 unit per day.

⇒ Time taken by 1 woman = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of 1 woman

⇒ Time taken = 70 ÷ (1/4) = 70 × 4 = 280 days

∴ The correct answer is 280 days.

Additional Information

Chain Rule (MDH Concept)

If M1 persons can do W1 work in D1 days working H1 hours a day, and M2 persons do W2 work in D2 days working H2 hours a day, then (M1 × D1 × H1) ÷ W1 = (M2 × D2 × H2) ÷ W2.

Concept of Efficiency

Efficiency is inversely proportional to time. If group A takes x days and group B takes y days, the ratio of their efficiencies is y : x.

Total Work using LCM

Assuming the Total Work as the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of the given time periods avoids fractional calculations initially and significantly simplifies finding individual efficiencies.

questions.question: A student purchased a box of pencils at the rate of ₹35 for 10 pencils and sold all of them at the rate of ₹54 for 9 pencils. In this transaction, he gained ₹350. How many pencils did the box contain?
questions.questionHtml: A student purchased a box of pencils at the rate of ₹35 for 10 pencils and sold all of them at the rate of ₹54 for 9 pencils. In this transaction, he gained ₹350. How many pencils did the box contain?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Profit on 1 pencil = (SP of 1 pencil) − (CP of 1 pencil)

Profit on 1 pencil = (54 ÷ 9) − (35 ÷ 10) = 6 − 3.5 = &inr;2.5

Total number of pencils = Total Profit ÷ Profit per pencil

Total pencils = 350 ÷ 2.5 = 140

∴ The correct answer is 140 pencils.

Alternate Method

Given:

Cost Price (CP) of 10 pencils = &inr;35

Selling Price (SP) of 9 pencils = &inr;54

Total profit gained = &inr;350

Calculations:

⇒ CP of 1 pencil = 35 ÷ 10 = &inr;3.5

⇒ SP of 1 pencil = 54 ÷ 9 = &inr;6

⇒ Profit earned on 1 pencil = SP − CP = 6 − 3.5 = &inr;2.5

⇒ Total number of pencils = Total profit ÷ Profit on 1 pencil

⇒ Total number of pencils = 350 ÷ 2.5

⇒ Total number of pencils = 140

∴ The correct answer is 140 pencils.

Additional Information

Basic Profit and Loss

Profit = SP − CP | Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.

Unitary Method

Finding the value of a single unit first (CP and SP of 1 item) simplifies comparing varying quantities.

LCM Method

Instead of the unitary method, making quantities equal by taking the LCM of given items (e.g., LCM of 9 and 10 is 90) helps avoid decimal calculations.

questions.question: A rectangular metal sheet is of length 24 cm and breadth 18 cm. From each of its corners a square of side x cm is cut off and an open box is made of the remaining sheet. If the volume of the box is 640 cubic cm, then what is the value of x ?
questions.questionHtml: A rectangular metal sheet is of length 24 cm and breadth 18 cm. From each of its corners a square of side x cm is cut off and an open box is made of the remaining sheet. If the volume of the box is 640 cubic cm, then what is the value of x ?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The dimensions of the open box formed will be (24 − 2x), (18 − 2x), and x.

Volume of the box = Length × Breadth × Height = x × (24 − 2x) × (18 − 2x)

By checking the given options, we can substitute x = 4 directly into the volume formula:

Volume = 4 × (24 − 2 × 4) × (18 − 2 × 4)

Volume = 4 × 16 × 10 = 640 cm3.

Since this perfectly matches the given volume, we do not need to check further.

∴ The correct answer is 4 cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

Length of the rectangular sheet = 24 cm

Breadth of the rectangular sheet = 18 cm

Side of the square cut from each corner = x cm

Volume of the open box = 640 cm3

Formula Used:

Volume of a cuboid = Length × Breadth × Height

Calculation:

⇒ When squares of side x are cut from the 4 corners, the remaining sheet is folded up to form an open box.

⇒ Length of the box (L) = 24 − 2x

⇒ Breadth of the box (B) = 18 − 2x

⇒ Height of the box (H) = x

⇒ Volume = (24 − 2x) × (18 − 2x) × x = 640

⇒ Taking 2 common from the first two terms:

⇒ 2 × (12 − x) × 2 × (9 − x) × x = 640

⇒ 4x × (12 − x) × (9 − x) = 640

⇒ x(12 − x)(9 − x) = 160

⇒ Since x must be less than 9 (otherwise breadth becomes negative or zero), we test the options.

⇒ If x = 4: 4 × (12 − 4) × (9 − 4) = 4 × 8 × 5 = 160

⇒ This satisfies the algebraic equation perfectly.

∴ The correct answer is 4 cm.

Additional Information

Valid Range for 'x'

Since dimensions cannot be negative, the cut side x must be strictly less than half of the smaller side of the rectangle. Here, 18 − 2x > 0 implies x < 9 cm.

Total Surface Area of Open Box

The outer surface area of the resulting open box is simply the original area of the rectangular sheet minus the area of the 4 cut-out corner squares: Area = (L × B) − 4x2.

Maximized Volume Concept

To find the specific value of x that maximizes the volume of such a box, we use calculus by setting the first derivative equal to zero (dV/dx = 0).

questions.questionHtml: Find the length of one side of a rhombus whose area is 24 cm2 and the sum of the lengths of its diagonals is 14 cm.
questions.solution:
According to the concept, PQ/2 = 24, so PQ = 48 (Equation 1). According to the question, P + Q = 14 (Equation 2).

Now, considering that O bisects BD and AC at a right angle, we have ΔCOD as a right-angled triangle at O. By applying the Pythagorean theorem, we find DC = 5 cm.

Therefore, each side of the rhombus is 5 cm.

questions.question: A car runs the first 272 km at an average speed of 40 km/h and the next 85 km at an average speed of 50 km/h. What is the average speed (in km/h) for the entire journey?
questions.questionHtml: A car runs the first 272 km at an average speed of 40 km/h and the next 85 km at an average speed of 50 km/h. What is the average speed (in km/h) for the entire journey?
questions.solution:
Time taken to cover the 272 km stretch = 272/40 = 6.8 hours

∴ The average speed for the entire journey is 42 km/h.

questions.question: Two consecutive numbers are such that one-fourth of the smaller number exceeds one-fifth of the larger number by 3. The larger number is ________.
questions.questionHtml: Two consecutive numbers are such that one-fourth of the smaller number exceeds one-fifth of the larger number by 3. The larger number is ________.
questions.solution:
⇒  \(x\over4\)   = \(x+1\over5\) + 3 ⇒ 3 = \({x\over4}-{x+1\over5}\)

⇒ 60 = x - 4, x = 64

questions.question: The compound interest accrued on an amount of Rs. 25,500 at the end of three years is Rs. 8,440.50. What would be the simple interest accrued on the same amount at the same rate in the same period?
questions.questionHtml: The compound interest accrued on an amount of Rs. 25,500 at the end of three years is Rs. 8,440.50. What would be the simple interest accrued on the same amount at the same rate in the same period?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of Amount to Principal for 3 years = (25500 + 8440.50) ÷ 25500 = 33940.5 ÷ 25500 = 1331 / 1000.

Equivalent ratio for 1 year = 3√(1331 / 1000) = 11 / 10.

Interest rate (R) = (11 − 10) ÷ 10 × 100% = 10%.

Simple Interest for 3 years = 30% of Principal = 30% of 25500 = 7650.

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 7650.

Alternate Method

Given:

Principal (P) = Rs. 25,500

Time (T) = 3 years

Compound Interest (CI) = Rs. 8,440.50

Formula Used:

Amount (A) = P(1 + R / 100)T

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Calculations:

⇒ Amount (A) = P + CI

⇒ A = 25500 + 8440.50 = 33940.50

⇒ 33940.50 = 25500 × (1 + R / 100)3

⇒ (1 + R / 100)3 = 33940.50 ÷ 25500

⇒ (1 + R / 100)3 = 339405 / 255000

⇒ (1 + R / 100)3 = 1331 / 1000 (dividing by 255)

⇒ (1 + R / 100)3 = (11 / 10)3

⇒ 1 + R / 100 = 11 / 10

⇒ R / 100 = 1 / 10

⇒ R = 10%

⇒ SI = (25500 × 10 × 3) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 255 × 30 = 7650

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 7650.

Additional Information

Effective Compound Interest Rate

For a 10% per annum rate, the effective CI for 2 years is 21%, and for 3 years, it is 33.1%.

Difference Between CI and SI (2 Years)

Difference = P × (R ÷ 100)2. It determines the extra interest earned through compounding over exactly two years.

Difference Between CI and SI (3 Years)

Difference = P × (R ÷ 100)2 × (3 + R ÷ 100). Essential formula for efficiently finding the three-year CI and SI differences without complete calculations.

questions.question: 4 years ago, the average age of a family of 4 members was 19 years. A baby having been born, the average age of the family is the same today. Find the present age of the baby.
questions.questionHtml: 4 years ago, the average age of a family of 4 members was 19 years. A baby having been born, the average age of the family is the same today. Find the present age of the baby.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Present average age of 4 older members = 19 + 4 = 23 years.

Total age of these 4 members today = 23 × 4 = 92 years.

Total age of 5 members today (including baby) = 19 × 5 = 95 years.

Present age of the baby = 95 − 92 = 3 years.

∴ The correct answer is 3 years.

Alternate Method

Given:

Average age of a family of 4 members 4 years ago = 19 years

Current average age of the family (5 members including baby) = 19 years

Formula Used:

Total Age = Average Age × Number of Persons

Calculations:

⇒ Total age of 4 members 4 years ago = 4 × 19 = 76 years

⇒ After 4 years, each member's age increases by 4 years.

⇒ Total increase in age of 4 members = 4 × 4 = 16 years

⇒ Present total age of the 4 original members = 76 + 16 = 92 years

⇒ Total members in the family today = 4 + 1 (baby) = 5 members

⇒ Present total age of 5 members = 5 × 19 = 95 years

⇒ Present age of the baby = Total present age of 5 members − Total present age of 4 members

⇒ Present age of the baby = 95 − 92 = 3 years

∴ The correct answer is 3 years.

Additional Information

Change in Average over Time

If the average age of a group is A years, then after t years, the new average age of the same group becomes (A + t) years, provided no member leaves or joins.

Inclusion of a New Member

Age of new member = Total age of new group − Total age of old group at present. This is frequently used when a baby is born or a new person joins a group.

Combined Average

The combined average of two groups with sizes n1 and n2 and averages A1 and A2 respectively is given by (n1A1 + n2A2) ÷ (n1 + n2).

questions.question: In a right circular cylinder, the radius of the cylinder is 7 m. If the curved surface area of a right circular cylinder is 75% of the total surface area of the right circular cylinder, then find the volume of the cylinder. (in m 3 )
questions.questionHtml: In a right circular cylinder, the radius of the cylinder is 7 m. If the curved surface area of a right circular cylinder is 75% of the total surface area of the right circular cylinder, then find the volume of the cylinder. (in m<sup>3</sup>)
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of Curved Surface Area (CSA) to Total Surface Area (TSA) of a cylinder = h / (h + r)

Given, CSA = 75% of TSA ⇒ h / (h + 7) = 3 / 4

⇒ 4h = 3h + 21 ⇒ h = 21 m

Volume = πr2h = π × 72 × 21 = 1029π m3

∴ The correct answer is 1029π m3.

Alternate Method

Given:

Radius of the right circular cylinder (r) = 7 m

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 75% of Total Surface Area (TSA)

Formula Used:

CSA of cylinder = 2πrh

TSA of cylinder = 2πr(h + r)

Volume of cylinder = πr2h

Calculation:

⇒ 2πrh = (75 / 100) × 2πr(h + r)

⇒ h = (3 / 4) × (h + 7)

⇒ 4h = 3h + 21

⇒ h = 21 m

⇒ Volume of the cylinder = π × (7)2 × 21

⇒ Volume = π × 49 × 21

⇒ Volume = 1029π m3

∴ The correct answer is 1029π m3.

Additional Information

Volume of a Right Circular Cone

The volume of a cone is exactly one-third the volume of a cylinder with the same base radius and height: V = (1/3)πr2h.

Total Surface Area of a Cylinder

TSA is the sum of the curved surface area and the area of the two circular bases: TSA = 2πrh + 2πr2 = 2πr(h + r).

Hollow Cylinder Volume

For a hollow cylinder with an outer radius R and an inner radius r, the volume of the material used is calculated as: V = π(R2 − r2)h.

questions.question: Two children are running on a circular track 200 m long. They started from the same spot and in the same direction at speeds of 10 km/h and 8 km/h. How long will it take for them to meet?
questions.questionHtml: Two children are running on a circular track 200 m long. They started from the same spot and in the same direction at speeds of 10 km/h and 8 km/h. How long will it take for them to meet?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Checking for opposite directions, time = 200 ÷ (18 × 5/18) = 40 seconds (not given in options).

Thus, they are running in the same direction.

Relative speed = 10 − 8 = 2 km/h = 2 × (5/18) = 5/9 m/s.

Time to meet = Distance ÷ Relative speed = 200 ÷ (5/9) = 360 seconds.

Convert to minutes: 360 ÷ 60 = 6 minutes.

∴ The correct answer is 6 minutes.

Alternate Method

Given:

Length of circular path = 200 m

Speed of first child = 10 km/h

Speed of second child = 8 km/h

Formula Used:

Time taken to meet = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

Relative speed (same direction) = Speed1 − Speed2

Conversion from km/h to m/s = Multiply by 5/18

Calculations:

⇒ If they run in opposite directions, relative speed = 10 + 8 = 18 km/h = 18 × (5/18) = 5 m/s.

⇒ Time to meet = 200 ÷ 5 = 40 seconds (This is not among the given options).

⇒ Therefore, they must be running in the same direction.

⇒ Relative speed = 10 − 8 = 2 km/h

⇒ Relative speed in m/s = 2 × (5/18) = 5/9 m/s

⇒ Time taken to meet = Distance ÷ Relative speed = 200 ÷ (5/9)

⇒ Time = (200 × 9) ÷ 5 = 1800 ÷ 5 = 360 seconds

⇒ Converting seconds to minutes = 360 ÷ 60 = 6 minutes

∴ The correct answer is 6 minutes.

Additional Information

Meeting for the first time anywhere on the track

Time taken to meet for the first time = Length of track ÷ Relative speed.

Meeting for the first time at the starting point

Time taken = LCM of times taken by each individual to complete exactly one round independently.

Number of distinct meeting points

If the ratio of speeds is a : b (in simplest reduced form), the number of points is |a − b| for the same direction, and a + b for opposite directions.

questions.question: A and B together can do a piece of work in 18 days. B and C together can do the same work in 24 days and A and C together can do the same work in 27 days. In how many days will A, B and C complete the entire work, working together?
questions.questionHtml: A and B together can do a piece of work in 18 days. B and C together can do the same work in 24 days and A and C together can do the same work in 27 days. In how many days will A, B and C complete the entire work, working together?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total Work = LCM(18, 24, 27) = 216 units.

Efficiency of (A + B) = 216 ÷ 18 = 12 units/day

Efficiency of (B + C) = 216 ÷ 24 = 9 units/day

Efficiency of (A + C) = 216 ÷ 27 = 8 units/day

Total efficiency of 2(A + B + C) = 12 + 9 + 8 = 29 ⇒ (A + B + C) efficiency = 29 ÷ 2 = 14.5 units/day.

Time taken by A, B, and C = 216 ÷ (29 / 2) = 432 / 29 = 14 26/29 days.

∴ The correct answer is 14 26/29 days.

Alternate Method

Given:

Time taken by (A + B) = 18 days

Time taken by (B + C) = 24 days

Time taken by (A + C) = 27 days

Formula Used:

Total Work = Time × Efficiency

Time Taken = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency

Person Days Total Work Efficiency
A + B 18 216 12
B + C 24 9
A + C 27 8

Calculations:

⇒ Adding all efficiencies: (A + B) + (B + C) + (A + C) = 12 + 9 + 8

⇒ 2(A + B + C) = 29 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of (A + B + C) = 29 ÷ 2 units/day

⇒ Total time taken by A, B and C working together = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of (A + B + C)

⇒ Time taken = 216 ÷ (29 / 2)

⇒ Time taken = (216 × 2) / 29 = 432 / 29

⇒ Time taken = 14 26/29 days

∴ The correct answer is 14 26/29 days.

Additional Information

Pipes & Cisterns

Works on the same concept as time and work, but inlet pipes have positive efficiency while outlet pipes (leaks) have negative efficiency. Total capacity replaces total work.

Work & Wages

Wages are strictly distributed in the ratio of the actual work done by each person. If all workers operate for the same number of days, wages are divided in the ratio of their efficiencies.

Alternate Day Work

When individuals work on alternate days, calculate the work done in one complete cycle (e.g., 2 days) and multiply it to get as close to the total work as possible before calculating the final remainder.
